labs.title: One product, four perspectives
labs.objective: Distinguish application, system, platform, and ecosystem in one case.
labs.intro: P0 example: the portfolio and learning site share a repository. Change the analytical perspective: the code stays the same but your boundary changes.
labs.assumption: Conceptual example: a shared repository does not prove a platform exists; it needs capabilities and real consumers.

outcomes.title: Application: experience
outcomes.cause: You want visitors to explore completed work.
outcomes.mechanism: The boundary covers the visitor interface and tasks, not the entire publishing system.
outcomes.effect: Evaluate portfolio navigation, content and accessibility.

outcomes.title: System: collaboration
outcomes.cause: You want to explain how a session is published.
outcomes.mechanism: The boundary includes sources, validation, rendering, HTML output and delivery.
outcomes.effect: You can trace pipeline failures without calling each component a platform.

outcomes.title: Platform: reusable capability
outcomes.mechanism: Consider editorial contracts, a renderer, compatibility and identifiable consumers.
outcomes.effect: Justify the shared capability by actual adoption, not repeated folders.

outcomes.title: Ecosystem: actors and dependencies
outcomes.mechanism: Include authors, learners, browser, hosting and external standards.
outcomes.effect: Consider constraints and failures beyond the internal modules.

labs.title: Explore change propagation
labs.objective: Compare illustrative change-propagation scenarios and explain why modifying one component may require reviewing others, without attributing unverified dependencies to the repository.
labs.intro: Compare two hypothetical scenarios. In the first, a required field in the editorial contract changes, revealing potential review points. In the second, the portfolio's professional copy changes. Observe how responsibilities and contracts determine what should be inspected. These scenarios do not represent an executed analysis of the real dependency graph.
labs.assumption: The diagrams represent static conceptual examples, not verified repository dependencies. They do not compute actual reachability or highlight nodes as affected consumers. Potential review points are not observed failures or mandatory changes. Only source-code inspection and tests can confirm the effective impact.

outcomes.title: Contract change: inspect consumers
outcomes.mechanism: Validator, renderer and generated output might require coordinated migration; compatibility needs checking.
outcomes.effect: Check contract, content and tests. The portfolio should not depend on this schema.

outcomes.title: Local editorial change: boundary preserved
outcomes.mechanism: The change belongs to the portfolio app rather than the session contract.
outcomes.effect: Check its view and links; do not infer that no general build will run.

labs.title: What changes when JavaScript cannot run?
labs.objective: Predict text availability given delivery strategy and JavaScript execution.
labs.intro: Change two variables in a hypothetical case: where the text is created and whether JavaScript runs. Compare the mechanism to its effect, not to a quality percentage.
labs.assumption: This model only covers the potential presence of text in the DOM; it does not calculate WCAG accessibility, load times, or network reliability.

outcomes.title: Text available, progressive enhancement
outcomes.mechanism: The browser can read existing text; JS enhances controls without being the sole source.
outcomes.effect: Theory is readable; controls require independent tests.

outcomes.title: Text available without JavaScript
outcomes.mechanism: No code needs to insert lesson text into the document.
outcomes.effect: Theory remains readable even when controls cannot save study marks.

outcomes.title: Content depends on a script
outcomes.cause: Text created only by JS, and execution is available.
outcomes.mechanism: The script must load and run to create the lesson DOM.
outcomes.effect: Content might appear; successful script execution is not guaranteed by this model.

outcomes.title: Text absent, constraint violated
outcomes.cause: Text created only by JS, and execution is unavailable.
outcomes.mechanism: Nothing inserts the lesson text into the document.
outcomes.effect: The solution violates the requirement for theory readable without JavaScript.

labs.title: May the AI-assisted draft proceed?
labs.objective: Justify an AI product boundary through permission, verification and human review.
labs.intro: Hypothetical example: an assistant proposes a document summary. Change the conditions and observe the exercise rules. No data is sent to external services.
labs.assumption: Teaching rules, not universal policy, legal advice, or a real security evaluation. Passing these controls does NOT authorize publication.

outcomes.title: Stop transfer
outcomes.mechanism: Permission checks precede transfer or generation; accurate citations cannot override this block.
outcomes.effect: Do not send data. Seek a non-AI alternative or obtain authorization.

outcomes.title: Do not publish unsupported claims
outcomes.mechanism: Fluent writing does not demonstrate that claims are supported.
outcomes.effect: Validate evidence before presenting the content as fact.

outcomes.title: Keep it as a draft
outcomes.cause: Authorized input, checked citations, no reviewer.
outcomes.mechanism: Checked citations do not replace a human editorial decision.
outcomes.effect: Do not auto-publish under these rules.

outcomes.title: Ready for editorial review
outcomes.cause: Authorized input, checked citations and reviewer available.
outcomes.mechanism: The exercise minimums permit considering the draft, not proving final quality.
outcomes.effect: A human must decide. Nothing is automatically published.
